_comment: Scoring rules for filter/mail-filter.js.
A message is junked when total >= threshold AND it scored in >= minCategories
distinct categories. Requiring two categories is what stops a single unlucky word
from junking real mail: 'Israel' alone scores 2 in one category and goes nowhere.
Patterns are JS regex source, matched case-insensitively against subject + body.
Keep them literal — no nested quantifiers (catastrophic backtracking on a 1 MB body).
Per-box override: put a copy at /etc/cocx/mail-filter-rules.json (cocx points MAIL_FILTER_RULES at it).
The account's own domain is always allowed (MAIL_FILTER_ALLOW_OWN_DOMAIN=0 disables);
allowFromDomains is for OTHER trusted domains.
_quoteMarkersComment: Where the carrier's own words end and quoted third-party text begins. Everything
from the FIRST match onward is scored at the global quotedCap instead of full
weight — see the split in classify(). Matched multiline, case-insensitively.

advance_fee._comment: The money-movement skeleton every 419 shares, whatever the pretext.

appeal._comment: The trust-building opener. Weak alone, decisive in combination.

_comment: The rotating geopolitical pretext (Nigeria -> Syria -> Ukraine -> Gaza).
SUPPORTING evidence only: capped at 4 — BELOW the threshold on purpose, so this
category can never reach a verdict without corroboration. minCategories means a
hits nothing but this can never be junked. That is deliberate — a real press or
personal email may name a conflict, and news words are not a spam signal.
Unsolicited SEO/backlink/web-design pitches — the other half of what a public
admin@ receives. Patterns are taken from the real messages that arrived, not
from memory: the first draft matched 'I visited your website' and missed the
actual 'I recently reviewed your <domain>', scoring 3 instead of a verdict.
solo:true because a pitch that trips three distinct patterns needs no
corroboration — unlike crisis_pretext, which must never convict alone.
patterns: i (visited|came across|stumbled upon|was browsing|recently reviewed|reviewed|looked at|analy[sz]ed) your
if you( a|')re interested,? (let me know|reply|please)
